rule: The conjunction -na means 'and', connects two clauses, occurs after one of the first words of the second clause, and is written attached to that word.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Contrastive Somali Grammar for Mother Tongue Speakers (University of Gothenburg, 2022), p. 45
source_note: The grammar explicitly describes -na as a clause-connecting conjunction and its attached orthography.

rule: ayaana can be the noun-focus particle ayaa followed by the conjunction -na 'and'.
source: Martin Orwin, Colloquial Somali, lesson text/vocabulary around p. 73
source_note: The vocabulary gloss explicitly identifies ayaana as 'focus marker ayaa + na, and'.

rule: baana is focus + conjunction, roughly 'and ... FOCUS'.
source: R. David Zorc, Somali-English Dictionary, revised 2019; Somali Reference Grammar index
source_note: Zorc lists baana as 'focus + conj' and 'and ... FOCUS'.

rule: When ayaana/baana has a true focused subject immediately before it, removing only connective -na leaves the ordinary ayaa/baa subject-focus construction; reviewed common-noun focused subjects therefore keep the absolute/non-subject surface and restrictive agreement rules already established for subject focus.
source: CONN-FOCUS-001/002/003 plus existing project subject-focus evidence
project_execution: Normalize ayaana->ayaa and baana->baa only inside an independently established second-clause connective context, then delegate case/agreement to existing subject-focus analyzers.

rule: ayaana is not negative ayaan. The first executable stage does not infer negative+connective compounds or subject-clitic+connective forms such as buuna/beyna from ayaana/baana.
source: Morphological decomposition from Gothenburg/Orwin/Zorc plus project negative-focus ambiguity policy
project_execution: Require overt second-clause context for ayaana/baana. Standalone ayaana/baana, negative connective combinations, and clitic-bearing connective focus forms remain unjudged until separately modeled.
